_comment: Street RBA calls (economists and strategists). Update when an institution changes its view. For each bank: next_meeting = the RBA decision date the call refers to; call = hike | no change | cut; next_change = {month: YYYY-MM, optional label for approximate timing e.g. 'Mid 2027', direction: hike | cut, size_bp, rate_after}; as_of = date of the source; sources = links, newest first (the call bubble on the page links to sources[0], so put the article the current call comes from first). Set call to null if the bank has not published a view for the next meeting.

banks.note: Savings.com.au (24 Nov): all four majors expect the RBA to hold in December; CBA still forecasts the first cut in August 2027. Earlier: Belinda Allen (CommBank, MPA 19 Nov, after October jobs data with unemployment at 4.9%): 'An on-hold decision in December is locked in for the RBA'; the data 'does tip the balance closer to even' between the next move being a hike or cut. Cuts remain pencilled in for August and November 2027. Earlier, Ashwin Clarke (18 Nov): growth to slow enough 'to stay the RBA's hand in H1 2027'

Savings.com.au (24 Nov): all four majors expect a December hold; Westpac still forecasts the first cut in August 2027 and maintains the RBA 'has finished hiking rates in the current cycle'. Earlier: Westpac (Pound Sterling Live, 20 Nov, after October jobs data with unemployment at 4.9%): 'The data directly challenges the RBA's assessment that the labour market is "a little tight", reinforcing our view that it is done hiking'; peak unemployment forecast raised to 5.2% by mid-2027. Luci Ellis (13 Nov): RBA likely to pause in December; 'A rate hike in February 2027 cannot be ruled out but it is looking even less likely'. Cuts seen from August 2027 (Canstar via PropertyUpdate, 20 Nov)

Savings.com.au (24 Nov): all four majors expect a December hold; NAB still forecasts the first cut in August 2027 and maintains the RBA 'has finished hiking rates in the current cycle'; Taylor Nugent expects October 'to mark the peak for headline inflation'. Earlier: Sally Auld (NAB chief economist, National Forward View via Australian Conveyancer 23 Nov): 'With policy having been tightened to 4.85 per cent, rates are now clearly restrictive' and 'The balance between growth and inflation risks has shifted and we think the RBA is done hiking'; NAB expects the RBA to hold next month (December). Taylor Nugent (19 Nov, after October jobs data): a 25bp cut likely won't come until about August 2027

Adam Boyton (ANZ, Savings.com.au 24 Nov, October CPI preview): ANZ has brought its first cut forward to June 2027 (25bp to 4.60%), followed by cuts in August 2027 and February 2028 to 4.10%; 'a weaker labour market and a softer demand environment will help to lower inflation, despite cost pressures', though a June cut is 'unlikely' if underlying inflation stays above target. All four majors expect a December hold. Earlier, Madeline Dunk (19 Nov): 'The numbers do make it harder to see the case for the RBA hiking in December'

Shane Oliver (AMP weekly update for the week of 20 Nov, via Livewire; page undated): RBA 'likely to remain on hold at the December meeting as it assesses the recent flow of data and then remain on hold into next year'; 'we had been thinking that the RBA would not start cutting until November next year, but the weakening jobs market mean it could now come earlier say around August'. Recession risk put at 'a high and still rising 40%'. 25bp cut size assumed

George Tharenou (UBS, Reuters via Business Recorder 19 Nov, after October jobs data): 'We now expect the first rate cut of -25bps in Aug-27 (was Nov-27)' and 'an easing cycle of -75bps (was -50bps)'; UBS no longer expects further hikes (Market Index, 20 Nov). December hold inferred

Goldman Sachs (Pound Sterling Live, 20 Nov, new outlook; analyst not named): cash rate held at 4.85% 'until the fourth quarter of 2027', then lowered to 3.6% by end-2028; market pricing of about 4.4% called 'too hawkish'. Earlier (17 Nov): says the cash rate has peaked. December hold inferred. Month (November, first Q4 2027 meeting) and 25bp first-cut size assumed

Tim Hext (19 Nov): no explicit December call; 'The Reserve Bank is achieving much earlier than expected what it set out to do with the five rate hikes this year' and 'will be cautious until inflation starts turning'; notes markets price a full cut by August 2027 and 'If rate cuts begin next year the cycle will be deeper than just two cuts'. No own timing published. Earlier, Steve Campbell (3 Nov): 'Further tightening can't be ruled out'
